bars.name: Apollo Bar Ginza
bars.address: B1F MEIKO Building, 8-2-15 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shimbashi (JR / Tokyo Metro), 5 min walk
bars.description: I went down to this basement alone and ended up spending hours with the bartender on samurai films, whiskey, and music. By now he's an old friend: a man who loves old movies and, as far as I'm concerned, a modern-day samurai. The room is dim and New York in style, the tonic is house-made, and the whiskey shelf is worth the trip by itself. Expect a ¥1,000 cover and very little English. Closed Sundays and holidays. It's a bar you walk into alone, and it doesn't leave you that way.

bars.name: Star Bar Ginza
bars.address: B1F MODERNS GINZA, 1-5-13 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Ginza (Tokyo Metro Ginza/Marunouchi/Hibiya), 3 min walk
bars.description: The ice was the first thing I noticed. It's cut by hand with knives made from Japanese sword steel until it nearly disappears in the glass. I ordered the Sidecar, because that's Hisashi Kishi's drink: brandy, curaçao and lemon, shaken hard and poured over a single hand-cut cube. Kishi holds a world title from the International Bartenders Association and a Medal of Honor from the Emperor. Dim room, nineteen seats, no smoking. ¥1,100 charge, and plan on ¥6,000 or more. Open 5:00 to 11:30 every night. Friends can take a table; I'd sit at the counter alone and watch.

bars.name: Tír na nÓg
bars.address: B1F Cheers Ginza, 5-9-5 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo 104-0061
bars.station: Higashi-ginza (Tokyo Metro Hibiya / Toei Asakusa), 3 min walk
bars.description: Tír na nÓg is the Irish land of eternal youth, and this Ginza basement takes the name seriously: an iron sprite, a key hanging from the ceiling, butterflies, vials of colored fairy dust, gargoyles watching over the room. The cocktails are just as theatrical, some made with cotton candy, with names like the Fairytail Mule and Old Man Milin's Sour. It's a café until 5:00 with a ¥500 charge, then a bar until 4:00 in the morning with a ¥1,000 charge, tax included. Plan on ¥2,000 to ¥6,000, three minutes from Higashi-ginza. I'd bring somebody.

bars.name: New York Bar
bars.address: 52F Park Hyatt Tokyo, 3-7-1-2 Nishishinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shinjuku (JR / Tokyo Metro / Odakyu / Keio), 10 min walk
bars.description: Fifty-two floors up in the Park Hyatt, this is the bar from Lost in Translation, where two strangers who came alone find each other. The hotel closed for nineteen months and reopened in December 2025 with the windows and the live jazz where they were. Get there between 5:00 and 6:30 and there's no cover. After that it's ¥3,300 a person, and the first set starts at 6:30. No reservations, and no shorts, sandals or sleeveless shirts. Open until midnight. I'd go early on a weeknight, alone, and take a window seat.

bars.name: Bar Cocktailbook Shinjuku
aliases: バー カクテルブック 新宿
bars.address: 2F Plaza Nishishinjuku, 7-5-5 Nishishinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shinjuku (JR / Tokyo Metro / Odakyu / Keio), 5 min walk
bars.description: Akira has run this second-floor bar north of Shinjuku Station since 2011, after twelve years at a Shinjuku hotel bar, and his competition awards are on display. I got a warm towel when I sat down. There's no fixed list: he asks what you like and works from the season. When he made mine, he set a small pour of each spirit beside the glass so I could taste them on their own first. The matcha Old Fashioned is worth ordering. There are owls everywhere, because his wife loves them. About a dozen seats, ¥600 charge, closed Sundays and Mondays. A calm counter to sit at alone.

bars.name: KAKURETAI
bars.address: B1F Nakabayashi Building, 1-2 Arakicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Yotsuya-Sanchome (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi), 2 min walk
bars.description: A basement in Arakicho done up with mice and cheese. Yuta is behind the bar and treats you like a regular the first time you walk in. He makes seasonal fruit cocktails, pours Japanese whisky, and has an original watermelon cocktail. There's sofa seating, a designated smoking area, and a DJ every Friday. It's LGBTQ-friendly. Weeknights only, 8:00 to 1:00. It's small and fills up, so reserve. I'd come alone; nobody stays a stranger here long.

bars.name: Vowz Bar
bars.address: 2F AG Building, 6-42 Arakicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo 160-0007
bars.station: Yotsuya-sanchome (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi), Exit 4, 3 min walk
bars.description: The monks behind this second-floor counter in Arakicho are Jodo Shinshu priests, with monks from other sects on staff, and they've been pouring here since 2000. Every night there's a short service and a sermon. The cocktails are named for Buddhist heavens and hells: Gokuraku Jodo is the Pure Land, Aiyoku Jigoku is the hell of lust. The food is vegetarian, things like mock eel and miso-cured tofu. Ask, and a monk will sit with you at your table or give you advice on your life from across the counter. Plan on ¥2,000 to ¥5,000. Open 7:00 to 1:00, closed Sundays and holidays, three minutes from Yotsuya-sanchome. Come alone; you'll have someone to talk to.

bars.name: a BAR Sleeping Tales
aliases: ア バー スリーピング テイルズ
bars.address: B1F (right door) Towa Shinjuku Gyoen Co-op II, 2-1-14 Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shinjuku-Gyoemmae (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi), 3 min walk
bars.description: There's no menu. Toshi asked what I liked, looked at what was in season, and built something around it. The drink people ask for by name is the peanut-butter Old Fashioned. The basement is done up like medieval Europe, and it's counter seats only, so I watched every move. Take the right-hand door at B1F, near Shinjuku Gyoemmae Station. Open from 6:00 (5:00 on weekends) until 2:00, and until 3:00 on Fridays and Saturdays. Closed Wednesdays; book online. A good counter to sit at alone and let someone else decide.

bars.name: Golden Gai: Happy, BAR COO & OPEN BOOK
aliases: ハッピー ロッキンソールバー
bars.address: 1-1-6 to 1-1-8 Kabukicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shinjuku (JR / Tokyo Metro / Toei), 5 min walk
bars.description: Golden Gai is about two hundred tiny bars packed into the lanes off Kabukicho, and these are the three I'd send you to. Happy is a rock-and-soul bar on the third floor of the Maruha Building where you pick the records. BAR COO is Miya's counter, and she talks with everyone in fluent English. OPEN BOOK pours one thing, lemon sours, under the owner's grandfather's books. Bring friends and do all three.

subvenues.name: Happy (Rockin' Soul Bar)
subvenues.description: Third floor of the Maruha Building. You pull a record from the collection and it goes on, with more than a hundred drinks to go with it. About ¥900 cover, and the last Friday of the month is disco night. Sosuke, the owner, will talk music with you.

subvenues.name: BAR COO
subvenues.description: A handful of seats at street level. Miya runs it, speaks fluent English and some Japanese Sign Language, and puts regulars and travelers at the same counter. Ask her to surprise you. Closed Sundays.

subvenues.name: OPEN BOOK
subvenues.description: Kai Tanaka's grandfather was Komimasa Tanaka, the Naoki Prize winner who drank in Golden Gai nearly every day, and his books go up to the ceiling. The only drink is the lemon sour: brown-sugar shochu, syrup from domestic pesticide-free limes, sliced Hiroshima lemons, big ice, a thin glass. Fifteen people, all standing. No smoking, ¥300 charge, 8:00 to 11:55 every night.

bars.name: JANAI COFFEE
bars.address: B1F Yamanen Building, 2-3-13 Ebisuminami, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Ebisu (JR Yamanote / Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 3 min walk
bars.description: Getting in is half the night. I had to solve a riddle on their website just to reach the booking page, and reservations are online only. Down the stairs it looks like a coffee stand; show them the code and a bookcase swings open onto a dark bar. Half the cocktails have coffee in them and half don't, ¥1,400 to ¥1,600 each or ¥3,500 for a course of three. The staff speak English, the playlist is R&B, and they hand you a decaf on the way out. Twenty-eight seats, no smoking, 6:00 to midnight every day. Bring people; the riddle goes faster with help.

bars.name: A10
bars.address: B1F Bios Building, 1-12-11 Ebisunishi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Ebisu (JR Yamanote / Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 3 min walk
bars.description: Across from Ebisu Park there's a row of coin lockers. Pull on one and the whole wall swings open onto a stair down to the basement. Down there it's R&B, soul and jazz on vinyl through top-of-the-line sound, records up to the ceiling, and whoever is on the decks has been incredible every time I've gone; the DJ is the reason I keep coming back. There are twenty original cocktails, ¥1,430 to ¥1,980, plus a ¥1,100 seat charge. Thirty seats, open every night from 7:00 to 3:00; book ahead for weekends. Bring someone who hasn't seen the lockers open.

bars.name: Never Never Land
aliases: ネヴァーネヴァーランド
下北沢ネバーネバーランド
bars.address: 2F Yoshino Heights, 3-19-3 Kitazawa, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo 155-0031
bars.station: Shimokitazawa (Odakyu / Keio Inokashira), 3 min walk
bars.description: Never Never Land has been going in Shimokitazawa since 1978, on the second floor of Yoshino Heights, near Studio Noah. It moved here in the mid-2000s when its first building across the street came down. The walls are a patchwork of photos, fliers and posters for concerts and underground theater, and gigs happen now and then. The kitchen does Burmese-style curry and other spiced dishes, and the room is non-smoking. Plan on ¥2,000 to ¥3,000. Open 6:00 to 2:00 every night. Regulars and newcomers end up at the same tables; I'd go with friends.

bars.name: No Room For Squares
aliases: ノー・ルーム・フォー・スクエアーズ
bars.address: 4F Housing Kitazawa Building II, 2-1-7 Kitazawa, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shimokitazawa (Odakyu / Keio Inokashira), 3 min walk
bars.description: Named for the 1964 Hank Mobley album on Blue Note. You get in through the front of an old Coca-Cola vending machine on a fourth floor in Shimokitazawa. Inside are more than a thousand jazz records and no menu: you tell the owner what you like and the owner mixes it, mocktails included, with Ichiro's whisky on the shelf. Some nights there's live jazz. Twenty-two seats, cash only, no smoking before 6:00. Open 2:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m., days off vary. A good first bar to walk into nervous; I'd send you in alone.

bars.name: Bar sawa
bars.address: 1F Forum Nakameguro, 1-6-7 Higashiyama, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Nakameguro (Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 5 min walk
bars.description: Shigeko Shintani opened this Nakameguro whisky bar in 1985, and she and her staff have visited more than a hundred distilleries. There are over eight hundred whiskies behind the counter, including a 52-year-old Dalmore Sirius, one of twelve in the world, and Macallans from 1948 and 1951. Ten seats inside, more on the terrace, smoking allowed. ¥800 charge, half-price drinks from 5:00 to 8:00, open every night until 5:00 in the morning. Look for the yellow light over the door. I'd bring somebody who loves whisky and plan to spend more than I meant to.

bars.name: Gen Yamamoto
bars.address: 1F Anniversary Building, 1-6-4 Azabujuban, Minato-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Azabujuban (Toei Oedo), 3 min walk
bars.description: Eight counter seats and no menu, just a tasting course of small cocktails built on Japanese produce that follows the season. Plan on ¥8,000 to ¥10,000. The pours are small; the flavors are the point. No smoking. Booking is by phone only, up to seven days ahead, roughly noon to 3:00. Tuesday to Saturday, last entry 9:00, so this is where I'd start the night, alone at the counter.

bars.name: Bar Centifolia
aliases: バー センティフォリア
bars.address: 6F La Muse Azabujuban Building, 1-6-5 Azabujuban, Minato-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Azabujuban (Toei Oedo), 3 min walk
bars.description: Yuzo Komai opened this sixth-floor bar in 2017, and every drink is a performance. Some of it is art, some of it is Instagram. It's a fixed menu, with no classics and no substitutions: about ¥4,000 a drink, plus a ¥1,000 charge and tax. Drinks take time, and it's not a place to get drunk. Fourteen seats, smoking allowed, open 6:00 to 3:00 every night. I'd bring someone for an occasion.

bars.name: BAR &UNDER
aliases: バー アンドアンダー
bars.address: B1F Sotokanda Kanemura Building, 2-6-4 Sotokanda, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Akihabara (JR / Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 5 min walk
bars.description: A basement in Sotokanda managed by Koji Yamamoto, who worked his way from assistant director to director on TV variety shows before he started tending bar. He has created more than two hundred sake cocktails themed on characters, and about every two weeks there's a collaboration night with an anime or a YouTuber. He says the ampersand in the name means doing something together. About thirty seats, a crowd mostly in their twenties to forties, a ¥700 seat charge and a one-drink minimum. Open 6:00 to 11:00 on weekdays, from 4:00 on weekends and holidays, closed Mondays. Bring friends; that's the point of the name.

bars.name: NARU Jazz Livehouse
bars.address: B1F Jujiya Building, 2-1 Kanda Surugadai, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 101-0062
bars.station: Ochanomizu (JR Chuo/Sobu, Tokyo Metro Marunouchi), 1 min walk
bars.description: NARU has been open since 1969, a minute from the Bridge exit at Ochanomizu. The room is set around a grand piano along the back wall, and the band plays three sets a night: ¥2,500 covers all three, plus drinks. The food is generous and cheap for what you get. Smoking is allowed, except during some sets. Evenings, 7:00 to 10:00. I'd come with friends, though people who come alone get the same welcome.

bars.name: Game Bar A-Button
aliases: ゲームバー エーボタン
bars.address: 1F Dai-5 Mitsumasa Building, 1-13-9 Taito, Taito-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Inaricho (Tokyo Metro Ginza), 4 min walk
bars.description: Nagamine managed Sega arcades before he put his severance into this bar in 2008, in a former ramen shop east of Akihabara. It's packed with his own collection: consoles, controllers, figures, merchandise. Don't come expecting to play everything. After Japan's software copyright association started sending letters to game bars, he stopped keeping some makers' machines playable. Thirteen seats, nine at the counter. I'd go with someone who grew up on the same consoles.

bars.name: BAR Willow's
bars.address: 6F-E, 88 Building, 2-1-3 Ueno, Taito-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Okachimachi (JR), 3 min walk; Ueno-Hirokoji (Tokyo Metro Ginza), 1 min walk
bars.description: I don't visit Tokyo without coming here, usually several times a trip. Yanagisawa owns the bar and was chief bartender at the Yokohama Royal Park Hotel before this. He's about as attentive as a bartender gets, and his English is excellent. The ice is hand-crafted and priced like it, and that is what good service costs. Every chair is an antique, picked one at a time, and the chair in the logo means there's always a seat waiting for you. After enough trips, there is. Over two hundred whiskies, good alcohol-free cocktails, fresh coffee. Sixteen seats, groups of four at most. Tuesday to Saturday until 3:00, Sundays until 11:00, closed Mondays and holidays.

bars.name: Rock Bar Sakebi
aliases: ロックバー さけび
bars.address: 1F, 2-16-11 Negishi, Taito-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Uguisudani (JR Yamanote), 5 min walk
bars.description: Sakebi means scream. The room is completely dark except for a few strange lights, with ten seats at the counter and a sound system that earns the name. The playlist is mostly hard rock and heavy metal, with the odd detour. Drinks are cheap, a night runs ¥1,000 to ¥2,000, you can smoke, and you can't reserve. Five minutes from Uguisudani or Iriya. I'd go alone and let it be loud.

bars.name: Eigakan Jazz
bars.address: B1F, 5-33-19 Hakusan, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo 112-0001
bars.station: Hakusan (Toei Mita Line A3), 1 min walk
bars.description: Eigakan means cinema. Masahiro Yoshida started it in the seventies to screen 16mm films, Oshima, Imamura and the rest of the Japanese New Wave. When the old building came down, he moved to Hakusan and turned it over to jazz. He built the tube amplifiers and the speakers himself, the records turn on a sixties Denon and an eighties Micro, and there's a Hiroshima Mon Amour poster on the wall. It's free jazz, played loud. Twenty seats, cash only, smoking allowed, no reservations, ¥1,000 to ¥2,000 for the night. Tuesday to Saturday, 4:00 to 10:00, a minute from Hakusan Station. Come alone and listen.

bars.name: SAKEBARO Aoyama
bars.imageAlt: Sake and wine bottles behind two metal sake cups and a small dish of almonds on the SAKEBARO counter
bars.address: 1F MD Aoyama, 2-10-8 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0062
bars.station: Omotesando (Tokyo Metro Ginza/Hanzomon/Chiyoda), 8 min walk
bars.description: Members only, with screening to get in. Inside are a tin-cube counter, a tin piano that plays itself, LED walls that move from blue to red, and staff who can give you the brewery, yeast, and polish rate of every pour. Conversation stays hushed. Now and then there's a ticketed dinner for non-members; book online and they email you the address. You can walk into everything else in this guide. Not this one.
bars.note: Reservation or membership required. Arrange access well before you travel.

bars.name: Rokusan Angel (Burlesque Tokyo)
bars.address: B2F Roppongi Nittaku Building, 3-8-15 Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Roppongi (Toei Oedo / Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 5 min walk
bars.description: Formerly Burlesque Tokyo, two floors below street level in Roppongi. The themed shows change every week and run seventy to ninety minutes, and the performers work the crowd. It's booked for birthdays and celebrations, so bring people, and reserve early for front seats. Expect ¥8,000 to ¥10,000 each after the 15% service charge. Limited English.
